mechanism_narrative: The ongoing decline in WORKPLACES mobility signals weaker commuting and fewer spontaneous weekday shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC will stay below its recent level over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES remains at or below its current four-week average.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility within two weeks diverts discretionary time toward outdoor recreation and away from indoor retail visits, pushing RETAIL_REC down on a one-to-two week lag.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 3 points from one weekly mean to the next
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within two weeks after a week-over-week rise of at least 3 points in PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES move together, they jointly index commuting intensity; if both improve, retail footfall should rise over the next four weeks because more trips combine errands with shopping.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are above their recent four-week means.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while GROCERY_PHARM remains near baseline, more errands are completed near home and fewer discretionary retail trips are made, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next month.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 8 points for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 8 points and GROCERY_PHARM staying within 2 points of baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in TRANSIT below its current level indicates tighter movement conditions that suppress shopping trips with a short lag, so RETAIL_REC will fall within one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week after TRANSIT crosses below -16 points.

mechanism_narrative: In a holiday-shopping regime, a gradual lift in GROCERY_PHARM usually precedes broader store traffic, so higher essential-shopping mobility should translate into higher RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 28-day mean over the next 28 days when GROCERY_PHARM is at or above its recent average.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS keep rising while TRANSIT stays weak, outdoor leisure substitutes for mall visits and retail-recreation mobility will weaken over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises and TRANSIT remains below -14 points in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within two weeks after PARKS increases while TRANSIT stays below -14 points.

mechanism_narrative: Under reopening, a sustained improvement in WORKPLACES should spill over into discretionary retail through higher daytime activity and after-work shopping, raising RETAIL_REC over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES rises from its current four-week average.
